title: Death toll from Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre rises to 43 as allies meet in Brussels
dek: Seven people reported missing at Komyshuvakha have been found alive, but more than 30 may still be under the rubble. Ukraine's allies discussed security guarantees in Brussels, and the EU paid Kyiv EUR 4.36 billion.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The number of people confirmed killed when Russian bombs hit a school used as an aid distribution point, and a nearby shelter, in the village of Komyshuvakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region has risen to 43, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday, the fourth day of the search. Rescuers were still looking for more than 30 people believed to be trapped in the rubble, the Associated Press reported. None of the figures can be independently verified.

There was some good news from the site. Zaporizhzhia regional police chief Artem Kysko said seven residents who had been reported missing had been found "alive and uninjured", Euromaidan Press reported, citing the Ukrainian outlet NV; among them was a 56-year-old woman whom police traced on Thursday after her relatives contacted them. The dead include two emergency workers and four police officers, according to Interfax-Ukraine. Zelensky has called the bombing one of the deadliest attacks of the war.

## Talks in Brussels, money from the EU

As the search went on, Ukraine's lead negotiator, Rustem Umerov, held a second day of talks at NATO headquarters in Brussels on Thursday with officials from the US, the UK, France, Germany, the EU and NATO, AP reported. The World Bank and the US investment firm BlackRock also took part. Umerov said the talks covered post-war reconstruction, funding for 2027 and security guarantees from Ukraine's Western allies, and that the two sides "separately discussed the threats from Russia to Ukraine and all of Europe, as well as joint steps to counter them".

US envoy Jared Kushner wrote on X that the aim was to end the war and build a security architecture so that fighting "never starts again", AP reported. Zelensky said on X that "the negotiations must move forward at full throttle". He said late on Wednesday that he had spoken for 90 minutes with Kushner and Steve Witkoff, the US negotiators who are due to host Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi next week.

The European Commission on Thursday paid Ukraine EUR 4.36 billion from its EUR 90 billion Ukraine Support Loan: EUR 3.7 billion in budget support, released after Kyiv met 12 policy conditions, and EUR 658 million for drones, missiles, radars, electronic warfare systems and air defence ammunition. "As Russia continues its relentless attacks, Ukraine is about to start its fifth wartime winter," Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in the Commission's statement. The Commission said EUR 25.2 billion remains available to Ukraine for the rest of 2026.

The air war continued overnight into Thursday. Ukraine's air defences said they had shot down or suppressed 105 of 128 Russian attack drones; Russia's defence ministry said it had downed 496 Ukrainian drones over 13 Russian regions, Crimea and the Black and Azov seas, AP reported. More than 200 drones targeted Russia's Ryazan region, where the governor said one person was wounded and Russian media reported a fire at the oil refinery. In Russian-occupied Luhansk, Moscow-installed leader Leonid Pasechnik said a Ukrainian attack on a bus killed five people and wounded 13. Neither side's claims can be independently verified.

## How the toll has risen

The bombing took place on Monday, 2 November. Ukraine's emergency services first put the toll at 24, with five injured, Al Jazeera reported; AP then reported 26 dead, and Zelensky put it at 29 on Tuesday morning. The acting regional governor, Mykhailo Semikin, said later on Tuesday that 37 had been killed and that 48 people were missing. On Monday Semikin had said a police officer and two emergency service rescuers were among the dead. Zelensky put the toll at 40 on Wednesday and 43 on Thursday.

Latvia, which holds the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council in November, has called for an emergency meeting of the Council over Russia's strikes on civilians, including at Komyshuvakha, Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže said. No date for the meeting had been announced by Thursday evening. Overnight into Tuesday, Russia also launched a large drone and missile attack on Ukraine's power grid.

## What Ukraine says happened

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the first air strike hit the school, and that "there was a repeat strike with nine more bombs, directly on the shelter where people were gathered". He said Russian forces must have known that residents who had stayed in Komyshuvakha received aid at the site every week, and called the attack proof that Russia "does not want any kind of de-escalation".

Russia's defence ministry did not comment on the Komyshuvakha strike in reports seen by The Declaration. On Monday it said its forces had shot down 212 Ukrainian drones overnight. Moscow says it does not target civilians.

## Talks in Abu Dhabi

The US envoy Steve Witkoff announced on Monday, in a post on X, that the US would "bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi", to discuss "post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures, and ending the war", according to the Australian news agency AAP. The Kyiv Post reported that the talks are scheduled for 10 and 11 November. Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent the US; the heads of the Russian and Ukrainian delegations have not been named.

According to AAP, Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to the new three-way round after meeting Witkoff in St Petersburg about two weeks ago. The last US-mediated talks were held in February, before the US and Israel went to war with Iran. Those Brussels meetings on security guarantees were held on Wednesday and Thursday, before the Abu Dhabi round.

Zelensky said last week that he was ready to meet Putin in Türkiye, and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has offered to help restart talks. The Kremlin has not publicly set out its terms for the Abu Dhabi round.

## Why it matters for India

India has called throughout the war for dialogue and diplomacy, and has kept buying Russian crude oil, which has made it a target of Western pressure over Russia's energy revenues. Any agreement that eases sanctions or the war's pressure on energy and grain markets would matter for Indian fuel and food prices; a new wave of Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy, and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, would keep those markets tight.

## Where the two sides stand

Witkoff said the Abu Dhabi talks, on 10 and 11 November, will be working-level negotiations on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and next steps, The Moscow Times reported. The Kremlin has not yet confirmed the date. The Moscow Times noted that Putin continues to demand that Ukraine cede full control of the partly occupied Donetsk region before any ceasefire, a condition Kyiv has repeatedly rejected; Zelensky has resisted US pressure to give up territory in exchange for peace.

## What happens next

Ukrainian rescuers are still searching the site in Komyshuvakha, and with more than 30 people feared trapped the death toll may rise further. No date has been announced for the Security Council meeting Latvia requested. The Abu Dhabi talks are due on 10-11 November. The rest of the EU's 2026 money for Ukraine, EUR 25.2 billion, is due to be paid out by the end of the year.
